templates.source: Lorex official RTSP guide 'IP Cameras: Using Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) with your DVR/NVR' (lorex-help.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/72000640829): 'rtsp://<user>:<pass>@<ip>:<port>/cam/realmonitor?channel=<channelNo>&subtype=<typeNo> — subtype 0 = Main Stream'. Corroborated by lorextechnology.com official product manuals: LHV5100W RTSP Streaming section (lorextechnology.com/downloads/security-dvr/LHV5100W/manual/LHV5100W_EN_R1/sect1sect17.html) and DV800-Series RTSP Streaming section (lorextechnology.com/downloads/security-dvr/DV800-Series/manual-EN/sect1sect21.html), both quoting the identical URL template and noting subtype=0 for Main Stream.
Same three official Lorex sources as main stream (Freshdesk KB 72000640829; LHV5100W manual; DV800-Series manual): 'subtype 1 = Sub Stream — recommended when connecting over the Internet'.

notes: Lorex (formerly a FLIR brand, now independent) is a Dahua OEM for the vast majority of its IP camera and DVR/NVR product lines. The identical /cam/realmonitor RTSP path is documented directly in three official Lorex sources: the Lorex Help Center KB article (Freshdesk), the LHV5100W product manual, and the DV800-Series manual. Official template: rtsp://{user}:{pass}@{ip}:554/cam/realmonitor?channel=<N>&subtype=<N> — subtype=0 for main (mainstream), subtype=1 for sub (sub-stream). Channel numbering starts at 1. Some very old or niche Lorex units may use Hikvision firmware (/Streaming/Channels/) but this is unconfirmed by official Lorex documentation and treated as cross-brand contamination here. Default RTSP port is 554; some NVR products also support port 8554 (seen in leads) but 554 is the documented default.
